nrr-2026.title: National Risk Register 2026
nrr-2026.note: Plain-English summaries based on the named national scenarios. PDF pages count from the first file page and may differ from printed page numbers.

avon-somerset-2026.title: Avon and Somerset Community Risk Register 2026
avon-somerset-2026.note: Plain-English summaries checked against the local risk sections.

E48000001-001.text: Water flooding normally dry land from rivers, the sea, heavy rainfall, rising groundwater or reservoirs, potentially damaging homes and services.

E48000001-002.text: Severe weather such as high winds, heavy rain, snow, thunderstorms, heatwaves or extreme cold that threatens health and disrupts daily life.

E48000001-003.text: Diseases spreading between animals. Some can also infect people, with consequences for animal welfare, farming and public health.

E48000001-004.text: Illnesses spreading through people, animals, contaminated surfaces or food, or contact with infected bodily fluids.

E48000001-005.text: Serious incidents on roads, railways, in the air or at sea, caused by collisions, mechanical failures or extreme weather.

E48000001-006.text: Accidents at industrial sites that can harm people or the environment beyond the site boundary, including chemical and nuclear facilities.

E48000001-007.text: Disruption to electricity, gas, water, communications, fuel or food supplies, with knock-on effects because essential services depend on one another.

E48000001-008.text: Deliberate threats including terrorism and organised crime, considered in local emergency planning even where sensitive details are not published.

E48000001-009.text: Crimes exploiting digital systems, including hacking, data theft and online fraud, which can cause financial loss and interrupt services.

NRR26-001.text: A terrorist attack overseas that affects British nationals, potentially causing deaths, injuries and a need for support or repatriation.

NRR26-002.text: Terrorist violence linked to Northern Ireland, including attempts to destabilise the peace settlement and harm people or public services.

NRR26-003.text: An attack using an explosive device carried by a person, placed at a location, or transported in a vehicle.

NRR26-004.text: An attack in which perpetrators move through an area seeking victims, using methods such as vehicles, knives or firearms.

NRR26-005.text: A deliberate attack affecting ships, ports or other maritime activity, with potential harm to people and disruption to transport.

NRR26-006.text: A deliberate attack on the rail network or its passengers, potentially causing casualties and interrupting rail services.

NRR26-007.text: An attack on aircraft or aviation infrastructure intended to cause harm and disruption to air travel.

NRR26-008.text: An incident in which people are held or threatened to force demands, potentially for political or ideological purposes.

NRR26-009.text: The deliberate killing or attempted killing of a prominent public figure.

NRR26-010.text: An attack using chemical, biological, radioactive or nuclear material to harm people, contaminate an area or disrupt services.

NRR26-011.text: A physical attack on gas infrastructure that interrupts operations or supplies and may endanger people nearby.

NRR26-012.text: A cyber attack that damages or disrupts the digital systems used to operate gas infrastructure.

NRR26-013.text: A physical attack on electricity infrastructure, potentially damaging equipment and interrupting power supplies.

NRR26-014.text: A cyber attack on electricity systems that could disrupt the transmission network and cause a widespread power outage.

NRR26-015.text: A physical attack on a civil nuclear facility or related infrastructure, with potential consequences for safety and energy supplies.

NRR26-016.text: A physical attack on facilities used to produce, import, store or distribute fuel, potentially interrupting supplies and harming workers.

NRR26-017.text: A cyber attack that interrupts the production or distribution of fuel by disrupting the systems used by fuel suppliers.

NRR26-018.text: A physical attack on a government building or estate that threatens people, assets or the continuity of government services.

NRR26-019.text: A cyber attack on health or social care systems that interrupts services, compromises information or limits access to essential systems.

NRR26-020.text: A cyber attack on transport networks or operating systems that disrupts travel and the movement of people or goods.

NRR26-021.text: A cyber attack on systems supporting fixed-line, mobile or internet communications, potentially disrupting essential connections.

NRR26-022.text: A cyber attack on data centres or the infrastructure supporting digital services used by businesses, public services and individuals.

NRR26-023.text: A cyber attack on digital systems controlling water treatment or distribution that could interrupt water supplies or wastewater services.

NRR26-024.text: A cyber attack on policing systems that could interrupt police operations and the delivery of emergency services.

NRR26-025.text: Malicious interference with civil nuclear systems, including digital systems, that threatens safe operations or essential services.

NRR26-026.text: A malicious attack on financial infrastructure that supports transactions essential to the UK economy.

NRR26-027.text: A malicious attack on a retail bank that could prevent customers from accessing accounts, payments or other banking services.

NRR26-028.text: Major disruption to the undersea telecommunications cables carrying international internet and data traffic to and from the UK.

NRR26-029.text: Disruption of international routes used to transport oil, potentially affecting supplies, energy prices, production and wider trade.

NRR26-030.text: Interference intended to undermine or disrupt democratic processes in the UK, including the integrity of elections and public participation.

NRR26-031.text: The failure of a major adult social care provider, putting the continuity of care for people with support needs at risk.

NRR26-032.text: The insolvency of a major supplier whose failure could interrupt services essential to the public sector.

NRR26-033.text: The insolvency of a fuel-sector business, potentially disrupting the supply of fuel while its operations are closed, sold or transferred.

NRR26-034.text: A serious rail accident, such as a derailment, that could cause injuries, damage and disruption to train services.

NRR26-035.text: A major accident involving a large passenger vessel, such as a cruise ship, potentially requiring rescue and emergency support.

NRR26-036.text: A major release of pollutants into UK waters, for example oil spilled from a tanker, pipeline or offshore installation.

NRR26-037.text: A vessel accident that obstructs a major UK port and interrupts the movement of imports and exports.

NRR26-038.text: An accident involving dangerous materials whose release could seriously harm people, public safety or the environment.

NRR26-039.text: A serious aircraft collision, with potential loss of life, injuries and disruption to aviation.

NRR26-040.text: Malicious use of a drone that threatens safety or disrupts operations, including activity around an airport.

NRR26-041.text: The loss or degradation of satellite communications, remote sensing or other space-based services that support activities on Earth.

NRR26-042.text: The loss of positioning, navigation or precise timing services used by transport, communications and other critical systems.

NRR26-043.text: A simultaneous loss of fixed and mobile communications, potentially disrupting broadband, telephone connections and access to essential services.

NRR26-044.text: A failure of the national electricity transmission system causing widespread loss of power and disruption across other essential systems.

NRR26-045.text: Failure of part of the electricity distribution network, causing a power outage across a region rather than the whole country.

NRR26-046.text: A shortage of gas or electricity relative to national demand, requiring action to manage supplies and protect essential services.

NRR26-047.text: An accident involving civil nuclear facilities or activities that could release radiation and require measures to protect the public.

NRR26-048.text: A radioactive release from a nuclear facility outside the UK, with potential consequences for people or the environment in the UK.

NRR26-049.text: Exposure to radioactive material while goods are being transported, or after a radioactive source has been lost or stolen.

NRR26-050.text: A technological failure at a major retail bank that interrupts customers’ access to accounts, payments or banking services.

NRR26-051.text: A technological failure in critical financial market infrastructure that interrupts the systems used to process financial transactions.

NRR26-052.text: An accidental fire or explosion at a site handling significant quantities of flammable or explosive substances.

NRR26-053.text: An accidental release of toxic gas or chemicals from a major hazard site, potentially affecting people and the surrounding environment.

NRR26-054.text: An accidental fire or explosion on an offshore oil or gas installation that handles large volumes of flammable material.

NRR26-055.text: An accidental release of flammable fuel from an onshore pipeline that leads to a fire or explosion.

NRR26-056.text: An accidental release from a major hazard pipeline carrying flammable or toxic materials, potentially causing a fire, explosion or harmful exposure.

NRR26-057.text: The accidental release of a dangerous disease-causing organism from a laboratory, potentially exposing people outside its containment arrangements.

NRR26-058.text: The collapse or breach of a dam or reservoir, suddenly releasing large volumes of fast-flowing water into surrounding areas.

NRR26-059.text: Failure of water infrastructure that leaves a large population without drinking water and may exceed the capacity for alternative supplies.

NRR26-060.text: Food contamination by disease-causing organisms, potentially leading to widespread illness and the withdrawal of affected products.

NRR26-061.text: A major fire that threatens people, property or infrastructure. It may result from accidents, deliberate acts or natural causes.

NRR26-062.text: A major interruption to data infrastructure that makes digital services unavailable across multiple organisations or sectors.

NRR26-063.text: A digital technology failure that disrupts services, potentially affecting multiple organisations or sectors at national scale.

NRR26-064.text: Accidental damage to the high-pressure national gas transmission network that interrupts its operation or the delivery of gas.

NRR26-065.text: An uncontrolled fire burning vegetation such as grass, heathland, woodland, crops or scrub, potentially threatening communities and infrastructure.

NRR26-066.text: A volcanic eruption overseas whose ash or gases could affect the UK, including disruption to air travel.

NRR26-067.text: Ground shaking caused by movement within the Earth, potentially damaging buildings and infrastructure. Damaging earthquakes are uncommon in the UK.

NRR26-068.text: A natural disaster overseas, such as an earthquake, hurricane or tsunami, that creates humanitarian needs and affects British people or interests.

NRR26-069.text: A major disaster affecting a UK Overseas Territory that requires assistance and a significant response from the UK.

NRR26-070.text: Disturbances originating from the Sun that can damage or interrupt satellites, communications, navigation and other technologies.

NRR26-071.text: A period of strong winds and storm conditions that can threaten people, damage property and disrupt transport or essential services.

NRR26-072.text: A period of unusually high temperatures, potentially harming health and placing pressure on infrastructure and essential services.

NRR26-073.text: Very cold conditions or heavy snowfall that threaten health and disrupt transport, energy supplies and other essential services.

NRR26-074.text: Flooding of coastal land caused by high tides, low-pressure weather systems, large waves or storm surges.

NRR26-075.text: Flooding when rivers, streams or brooks overflow into surrounding land, often following sustained or intense rainfall.

NRR26-076.text: Flooding when rainfall exceeds the capacity of drains and water flows across the ground. It can occur far from rivers or the coast.

NRR26-077.text: A shortage of water following an unusually dry period, potentially worsened by high demand during hot weather.

NRR26-078.text: Air pollution at levels that can damage health, including short-term episodes when weather prevents pollutants from dispersing.

NRR26-079.text: A new disease-causing organism spreading rapidly around the world where people have little existing immunity.

NRR26-080.text: An outbreak of a newly recognised infectious disease that could cause many people to become ill and require an enhanced public-health response.

NRR26-081.text: A highly infectious viral disease affecting animals including cattle, pigs, sheep, deer and goats, with serious consequences for farming.

NRR26-082.text: A severe infectious influenza disease primarily affecting birds. Prolonged direct contact can also transmit infection to some mammals, including humans.

NRR26-083.text: A viral disease spread by midges that can be fatal to horses, donkeys and mules. It does not affect humans.

NRR26-084.text: A highly contagious disease of pigs and wild boar that can spread through infected animals, meat products or contaminated objects. It does not infect humans.

NRR26-085.text: An outbreak of a plant-disease bacterium that can infect many plant species and damage agriculture or the natural environment.

NRR26-086.text: An outbreak of emerald ash borer beetles whose larvae damage ash trees, weakening them and potentially causing them to die.

NRR26-087.text: Serious disorder involving conflict or violence that can threaten public safety. It may develop from unrest or an incident that triggers wider tensions.

NRR26-088.text: Action by workers in a dispute with employers, including strikes or working to rule, that can disrupt services or infrastructure.

NRR26-089.text: A sudden return of British nationals from overseas following a crisis, creating a need for reception, accommodation and support in the UK.

NRR26-090.text: A major interruption to the operation of the criminal justice system, including pressures that prevent its core functions from continuing normally.

NRR26-091.text: Deliberate disruption of space systems or satellite services on which communications, navigation, infrastructure and defence operations depend.

NRR26-092.text: An attack on a partner country outside NATO that leads to a request for UK assistance.

NRR26-093.text: An attack on a NATO ally or qualifying deployed forces that triggers consideration of NATO’s collective-defence commitment under Article 5.

NRR26-094.text: A conventional military attack on the UK mainland or its Overseas Territories, requiring a defence and wider emergency response.

NRR26-095.text: A state misunderstanding another state’s intentions and responding with a nuclear strike, without the UK or its allies being directly involved.

flooding.text: The national register distinguishes coastal flooding, rivers overflowing their banks, and heavy rainfall overwhelming drainage. These can affect people, buildings and essential services.

weather.text: Severe weather includes storms and strong winds, unusually high temperatures, and very cold conditions or snow. These can threaten health and disrupt services.

animal-disease.text: The national register describes serious animal disease outbreaks, including foot and mouth disease, avian influenza, African horse sickness and African swine fever. Their effects differ by disease.

infectious-disease.text: Infectious disease emergencies include a new disease outbreak or a pandemic spreading internationally. They can affect many people and place pressure on health and other services.

industrial.text: Industrial emergencies include fires, explosions or toxic releases at sites and pipelines handling hazardous materials. Consequences can extend beyond the immediate facility.

transport.text: National transport scenarios include serious rail accidents, aircraft collisions and large passenger-vessel accidents, with potential casualties and major disruption.

utilities.text: Essential-service failures can interrupt electricity, gas, drinking water, communications or fuel supplies. Because these systems depend on one another, disruption can spread between services.

terrorism.text: The national register describes deliberate attacks on people, public places, transport and infrastructure. Different attack methods can cause casualties and wider disruption.

cyber.text: Cyber attacks can compromise digital systems or information and interrupt services. National scenarios cover sectors including health, transport, communications, energy, water and policing.

physical-infrastructure-attacks.text: Physical attacks on essential infrastructure can damage facilities and interrupt gas, electricity, fuel or other services.

disruption.text: National societal risks include public disorder and industrial action. They can disrupt daily activities and the delivery of essential services.

notes: Local definitions take priority. National summaries use Direct crosswalk matches; related national background is separately curated and does not change or confirm the crosswalk. Unmatched entries remain explicitly unavailable.
